checks.title: ESXi version is on a vendor-supported release
checks.rationale: End-of-life ESXi builds no longer receive security patches.
checks.remediation: Upgrade ESXi to a currently supported major.minor release per VMware's lifecycle policy.

checks.title: SSH daemon is disabled in steady state
checks.rationale: Persistent SSH on ESXi is a top-tier attack surface; enable only during maintenance.
checks.remediation: vim-cmd hostsvc/stop_service TSM-SSH && chkconfig SSH off

checks.title: ESXi Shell (TSM) is disabled in steady state
checks.rationale: The ESXi Shell exposes direct command access; production hosts should disable it.
checks.remediation: vim-cmd hostsvc/stop_service TSM && chkconfig TSM off

checks.title: Lockdown Mode is enabled
checks.command: esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Net/EnableLockdownMode 2>/dev/null | awk '/Int Value:/ {print $3; exit}'
checks.rationale: Lockdown mode forces management through vCenter, reducing direct-host abuse.
checks.remediation: Configure lockdown mode (Normal or Strict) via vCenter > Host > Configure > Security Profile.

checks.title: Strict UEFI Secure Boot is enabled
checks.command: esxcli system settings encryption get 2>/dev/null | awk '/Require Secure Boot:/ {print $4; exit}'
checks.rationale: Secure Boot blocks unsigned VIBs from loading in the boot chain.
checks.remediation: Enable UEFI Secure Boot in firmware and 'esxcli system settings encryption set --require-secure-boot=TRUE'.

checks.title: NTP service has at least one server configured
checks.command: esxcli system ntp get 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '/Servers/ {print $2}' | tr -d ' '
checks.rationale: Accurate time is required for log correlation, certificates, and Kerberos.

checks.title: Welcome / login banner is configured
checks.command: esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Annotations/WelcomeMessage 2>/dev/null | awk '/String Value:/ {sub(/^[ \t]*String Value:[ \t]*/, ""); print; exit}'
checks.rationale: Pre-login banners provide legal notice and aid incident response.
checks.remediation: esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Annotations/WelcomeMessage -s "<your banner>"

checks.title: SuppressShellWarning is OFF (warnings should be visible)
checks.command: esxcli system settings advanced list -o /UserVars/SuppressShellWarning 2>/dev/null | awk '/Int Value:/ {print $3; exit}'
checks.rationale: Suppressing shell warnings hides indicators that management services are active.

checks.title: Manual: review esxcli network firewall ruleset list
checks.audit: Run 'esxcli network firewall ruleset list' over SSH. Confirm only required rulesets are Enabled. Common targets: vSphereClient, sshServer, dhcpv6, snmp.
checks.rationale: Each enabled ruleset opens a port set on the ESXi management interface.
checks.remediation: Disable unused rulesets: 'esxcli network firewall ruleset set --enabled=false --ruleset-id=<id>'.

checks.title: Manual: vCenter is the only management plane (no rogue ESX Admins)
checks.audit: From vCenter, review Host > Permissions. Confirm no unexpected AD groups have Administrator role on the ESXi host directly.
checks.rationale: Domain joins prior to ESXi 7.0 created an implicit 'ESX Admins' AD group that granted host admin; this is a known privilege-escalation vector.
checks.remediation: Remove 'ESX Admins' AD group from host permissions; manage via vCenter SSO roles instead.
